articles.title: Chris Eubank Jr sends five-word message for Ryan Garcia to beat Conor Benn in Las Vegas Zuffa Boxing showdown tonight
articles.summary: International Sports News: Chris Eubank Jr has made his feelings clear ahead of Conor Benn’s huge showdown with Ryan Garcia. The former rivals have a long and bitter history, bu.
articles.body: Chris Eubank Jr has made his feelings clear ahead of Conor Benn’s huge showdown with Ryan Garcia. The former rivals have a long and bitter history, but Eubank Jr appears to be firmly backing Garcia in their latest chapter. Garcia and Benn are set to meet on Saturday, September 12, 2026, at the T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas in a Zuffa Boxing bout. Eubank Jr has now sent a short but clear message to Garcia before the fight, showing his support for the American star.Eubank Jr posted a picture with Garcia on X ahead of the fight. The message is unlikely to surprise boxing fans given Eubank Jr’s history with Benn. Eubank Jr defeated Benn by unanimous decision in their first meeting in April 2025. Now, he will watch closely as Benn takes on Garcia in another major test.Chris Eubank Jr sends Ryan Garcia a message before Conor Benn fightConor Benn has now moved on to another major challenge. He will face Ryan Garcia in Las Vegas on September 12. The fight gives Benn the chance to make another statement on a major stage.Garcia, meanwhile, brings his own star power and an impressive record in professional boxing. The American has become one of the biggest names in the sport because of his speed, punching power and huge social media following.Eubank Jr’s backing adds another layer to the fight. His latest X post sends a simple message to Garcia, “Get the job done kid.”The post could add extra motivation for Garcia as he prepares for one of the biggest fights of his career.For Benn, the upcoming challenge is now straightforward. He must put aside the outside noise and focus on Garcia.A victory would give Benn a major boost after his loss to Eubank Jr. It would also strengthen his position in the sport and potentially set up more high-profile fights. Garcia, however, will have his own plans.The rivalry between Chris Eubank Jr and Conor Benn has been one of boxing’s most talked-about stories in recent years.Their first planned fight was scheduled for October 2022. However, the bout was cancelled after Benn returned an adverse finding for clomifene. The fight was eventually revived and took place at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in April 2025.Eubank Jr entered that contest as the more experienced fighter. Benn was unbeaten at the time and had built a reputation as a dangerous puncher. However, Eubank Jr gave a disciplined performance over 12 rounds.He won by unanimous decision. All three judges scored the fight 116-112 in his favour.The victory gave Eubank Jr bragging rights in the long-running rivalry between the two families. Their fathers, Chris Eubank Sr and Nigel Benn, had famously fought twice during the 1990s.With Eubank Jr publicly backing Garcia, all eyes will now be on whether he can deliver against Benn inside the T-Mobile Arena.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Big Blue View mailbag: Defensive alignments, expectations as season begins
articles.summary: The mail’s here! Questions, answers about the Giants with one day before the 2026 season-opening game.
articles.body:
Richard Vitto asks: I was hoping you could clarify how the defensive line actually gets set up. Most of the time it seems to me that they play only 2 down linemen with 4 linebackers. Maybe to start a game or a possession they use a true front seven but without really tracking I really don't think I see it that often. Can you give us a general sense of how often they are in a package with just 2 down linemen and extra dbacks? And when they are on that configuration who are the "starters" most often on the field?

Ed says: Richard, I could find and quote you numbers from last season. That, though, is pointless because the Giants have a new defensive coordinator and much different defensive personnel.

The "base" defense is considered a 3-4, with three down linemen with their hands in the ground. Again, though, that is kind of pointless. You will see some occasions where the Giants line up that way. You will see occasions where they line up with two down linemen and everyone else standing. You will see occasions where two edge defenders function as hand in the ground defensive ends, making the defense look like a traditional four-man front. You will see times when there is only one true defensive lineman. You will see times when there are none and an edge defender (probably Kayvon Thibodeaux ) functions as a pass-rushing nose tackle.

Teams play defense nowadays according to down-and-distance, game score, and the game clock. It is all situational. It is impossible to give you numbers on how often different packages are used until we actually see it.

That said, the guys I would consider true starters in the front are D.J. Reader, Shelby Harris , Arvell Reese, Tremaine Edmunds , Brian Burns , Abdul Carter , and Thibodeaux. The safeties are Jevon Holland and Tyler Nubin . Dru Phillips is the nickel cornerback. I couldn't tell you who the Giants will decided to start at the outside cornberbacks slots — it is some combination of Greg Newsome , Deonte Banks , Paulson Adebo .

John Brenner asks: It seems to me that the Giants have developed a troubling pattern over the last 10 or 15 years of not looking ready to play at the beginning of the season. I don't have the numbers in front of me, but my impression is that they've lost the overwhelming majority of their openers and several times they haven't just lost, but have looked completely unprepared.

Do the numbers and your own observations support that impression? If so, what do you think has caused it across different coaches and rosters? And do you see any reason to expect something different against Dallas on Sunday under John Harbaugh?

Ed says: John, have you not been reading the website? We have been covering this topic for months. In fact, we have been talking about it for years. I asked Brian Daboll about it before both the 2024 and 2025 seasons.

Peter Smyth asks: This last week has been fan-torture. I can't wait for this long, (but hope-filled), offseason to end and find out how good this team really is. National media, and even local writers and hosts are tempering expectations and predict slight or medium improvement. Often, they sound like they haven't been paying attention to our team and are just writing us off.

As a BBV zealot, I have convinced myself the G-men will go on a run this season like Washington in 2024 and the Pats in 2025. I'm asking you to be my Giants-fan-therapist. Am I nuts to strongly think this could be our year? Even a Super Bowl victory? Help me!

Ed says: Peter, you are certainly encouraged to be as optimistic as you want to be.

Something I keep saying, though, is that the kind of one-year turnaround the New England Patriots and Chicago Bears experienced last season are still the exception rather than the rule. I think if that is what you "expecting" in 2026, you are setting yourself up for disappointment.

Maybe it happens. I just wouldn't expect it to happen.

When I made my game-by-game predictions, the most optimistic predicition I could make is 9-8. I still believe that. Maybe the Giants win six games. Maybe everything falls their way, and they get into double-digits in the win column.

I feel better about this team because I know the track record of the guy who is now in charge. I just can't expect an overnight miracle. There is still a lot to be proven, and a lot of work to be done.

Doug Mollin asks: Saw a stat from Sharp Football that really caught my eye.

"The Giants were leading in games last year for more snaps than the following teams: Ravens, Chiefs, Bengals , Panthers , Vikings, Cowboys, Commanders, Browns, Buccaneers, Saints."

Along with blowing 5 double digit fourth-quarter leads, it really makes me think the Giants could make a bigger leap this year than many expect. Could have had 7 wins last year with a little better luck, better coaching, better execution. What chance do you give the Giants to surprise on the upside over the predicted 7 win total? Is 10 wins out of the question?

Ed says: Doug, as I said above, it's not out of the question. Neither, though, is being a six-win team. As I said above, I just wouldn't go into the season believing that it is automatic that John Harbaugh is going to turn the Giants into a 13-win team right away.

Art Stein asks: To your knowledge is there any exchange of information or knowledge between the Giants and Rutgers. Historically, do coaches from Rutgers ask questions or seek information from the Giants?

Ed says: Art, I don't know what kind of information you think Rutgers coaches might seek from the Giants. To my knowledge, there isn't anything other than the standard exchange of information about NFL Draft prospects.

John McGruther asks: Do you know any of the words which the offense are using for their play calls and instructions, under the new coaching staff? I always remember "Omaha" being heard in the Manning years.

Ed says: John, if I did that would be a problem. The rest of the NFL would know them, too.

Have a Giants-related question? E-mail it to bigblueview@gmail.com and it might be featured in our weekly mailbag.

articles.title: The Tailgate Tape: West Virginia vs. UT Martin
articles.summary: Everything you need to know on gameday.
articles.body:
Alright Mountaineer Nation, 1-0 and it feels good, doesn't it? If you missed last week, this is The Tailgate Tape, the thing I'm gonna do every Saturday to get you ready for the game. Where to watch, what time to show up, who we're playing, who to keep your eyes on. Basically what I'd tell you if you called me up asking "Hey man, what am I watching this weekend?" My backyard's already set up again, sausages and ribs going on the grill, my wife's baked beans, some fries, GameDay on in the background. Let's talk UT Martin.

Kickoff is Saturday, September 12 at 1 p.m. ET, back home at Milan Puskar Stadium. Heads up though, this one's not on cable. You need ESPN+ for this one, so get that squared away before kickoff or you'll be scrambling. Weather

Cooler one this week, high around 65, low near 49, 40 percent chance of rain. Nothing like the wet mess we tailgated through for the opener, so take the win and enjoy a more comfortable Saturday outside.

UT Martin's making their first ever trip to Morgantown. They're an FCS team out of the Ohio Valley Conference, coached by Jason Simpson. They just handled Chicago State 42-7 last week, so they're sitting at 1-1 and they're not walking in here shaken up or unsure of themselves. They brought in a big signing class this year too, 47 new guys, so this isn't some team just happy to be here. Doesn't change the fact that jumping from FCS up to a Big 12 opponent is a completely different level of football. We should be the better team on paper, and it's not close.

Thomas Ansley is the one I'd watch first. Dude ran for 118 yards and three touchdowns on just 16 carries last week, that's not a fluke, that's a guy who can hurt you if you let him get going. Their quarterback, Surber, threw for 222 yards in that same game, so this isn't a team that's only going to try and run it down your throat. And keep an eye on Carter out wide, three catches for 62 yards last week. If our coverage gets a little too comfortable because of who's on the other sideline, he's the guy who'll make us pay for it.

That's the Tape for this week. Don't sleep on this game just because of who it's against. What I want to see from us defensively is simple, contain their quarterback, don't let him scramble around and extend plays, especially on third down. Offensively, stay aggressive, keep the foot on the gas instead of playing it too safe. We do those two things, this one's not close. Let's get to 2-0.

articles.title: Saturday Rockpile: Mason Adams is giving the Rockies something to look at
articles.summary: Colorado Rockies news and links for Saturday, September 12, 2026
articles.body:
Mason Adams did not come to the Rockies with the pedigree of a top pitching prospect.

Acquired from the White Sox along with Carlos Vielma in exchange for Brenton Doyle , Adams arrived as an older arm with an injury history rather than a marquee prospect. At 26, he is pitching in the big leagues for the first time while still working his way back toward a full workload after Tommy John surgery.

It is impossible to know what he will ultimately become, but through four starts, the results are intriguing. Adams has struck out 22 batters in 18.2 innings, while allowing five home runs and plenty of hard contact.

Still, there is enough here to get excited about for a Rockies team desperate for pitching. And with four starts now under his belt, there is enough to start looking under the hood.

Adams has already shown six pitches in the majors: a four-seam fastball , sinker , cutter , curveball , sweeper and changeup .

None of them looks particularly elite on its own. What stands out is the variety — different speeds, different movement profiles, and enough options to change how he attacks hitters as the game progresses.

Even the three fastballs move differently enough that a hitter cannot treat them as the same pitch, and the velocity separation across the arsenal gives Adams another way to change the look. His four-seamer sits roughly 11 mph above his curveball, with the cutter falling in between.

Taken together, the arsenal fits the broader direction the Rockies have been moving on the mound, even if nothing in Adams' profile screams future ace .

The Rockies do not need Adams to become an ace. They need competent major-league pitchers — and a lot of them. So far, the way Adams has used his six-pitch mix suggests there may be enough for Adams to become a useful major-league starter.

What stands out more than the number of pitches in Adams' arsenal is how he changes the mix once hitters have seen him.

Bryan Torres provided one of the clearest examples against St. Louis , seeing five four-seam fastballs during a six-pitch walk the first time they met.

The second meeting lasted one pitch: another four-seamer, which Torres lined for a single.

The third plate appearance looked completely different.

Two curves. Two changeups. No fastballs.

A similar adjustment had shown up five days earlier in Atlanta , where Adams struck out Drake Baldwin twice using two different pitch progressions.

The usage by time through the order makes the pattern easier to see:

Adams has consistently changed his pitch mix once hitters see him again, though the specific adjustment has varied by start.

Atlanta and St. Louis make it easy to think Adams is following a simple script: show the four-seamer early, then shift toward the sinker once hitters come back around.

Detroit complicated that assumption. Instead of leaning harder on the sinker the second time through, Adams nearly doubled his curveball usage. The adjustment itself appears to be the point, not necessarily which pitch he turns to.

The swing-and-miss gives that approach some teeth, too, particularly with two pitches.

Through his first three starts, Adams' four-seam fastball generated a 27.8% whiff rate, compared with a league baseline around 21–22% for four-seamers. His curveball was even more impressive at 58.3%, compared with a major-league baseline around 29–31%.

Against Detroit, both generated a 33% whiff rate as Adams struck out five over five innings.

That is where the warning signs start to show.

Through his first three starts, only 36.1% of Adams' balls in play were on the ground, compared with a league rate around 44%. Nearly 64% were hit in the air.

The contact was not soft, either. Adams entered Friday with a 61.1% hard-hit rate, well above the league average of roughly 39%, while right-handed hitters had slugged .808 against him.

Those numbers come from barely 14 major-league innings and should not be treated as established trends, but they are difficult to ignore:

Batted-ball results through Adams' first three MLB starts. (Baseball Savant)

That is the early concern: when hitters make contact, too much of it has been hard and too much of it has been in the air.

Friday did not eliminate that problem. Riley Greene singled at 111.5 mph, Colt Keith hit a ball at 99.6 mph and John Peck hit one at 97.1 mph before Max Clark homered at 95.2 mph in the fifth.

After Clark's home run, Adams walked the next two hitters before getting Javier Báez to roll over a sweeper for an inning-ending double play, his second of the game. Seven of his 10 non-strikeout outs came on the ground.

The contact is still a warning sign, but Detroit offered a glimpse of what is possible when Adams can keep more of it on the ground.

The hard contact is real. The amount of air contact is real. The four-seamer cannot carry the arsenal by itself.

But Adams has already shown some swing-and-miss, and he has not attacked hitters the same way every time through the order. The ability to change the mix as hitters adjust is part of what makes these first four starts interesting.

Four starts are nowhere near enough to know where that leads. But for a rotation that needs competent major-league innings almost as badly as it needs upside, Adams is showing enough to suggest he could help raise the floor in 2027.

The Albuquerque Isotopes (69-73) battled back from an early three-run deficit and briefly took the lead in the seventh, but the pitching could not quite hold it in a 6-5 loss to the Reno Aces (63-78).

Roc Riggio got Albuquerque on the board with his fifth Triple-A home run in the third, and the Isotopes continued chipping away after falling behind 4-1. Edouard Julien and Chad Stevens drove in runs in the fourth before Nic Kent tied the game with an RBI single in the sixth. Sterlin Thompson then gave Albuquerque its first lead with a solo homer in the seventh, his 12th of the season.

Thompson finished 2-for-5 with the homer, two runs and an RBI and is now hitting .325 with a .989 OPS. Riggio went 3-for-4 with his homer and an RBI, pushing his OPS to .840. Julien added two hits and an RBI, while Kent also had two hits. Albuquerque finished with 12 hits and three walks, but went just 3-for-10 with runners in scoring position and left nine on base.

The pitching was leaky throughout. Patrick Weigel allowed two runs over two innings, pushing his season ERA to 7.38, while Mason Green gave up two more over four innings. Parker Mushinski surrendered the tying run in the seventh, moving his ERA to 3.38, before Jeff Criswell allowed the go-ahead solo homer to Aramis Garcia in the eighth and took the loss.

The Hartford Yard Goats (65-70) were held scoreless for seven innings before making a late push, but the comeback fell just short in a 4-3 loss to the Somerset Patriots (73-63).

Somerset built a 4-0 lead against Konner Eaton , scoring once in the first, once in the third and twice in the fourth. Eaton allowed four runs on six hits and three walks over five innings, striking out five and surrendering two home runs before Nathan Blasick and Hunter Mann combined for three perfect innings out of the bullpen.

Hartford finally broke through in the eighth when Jack O'Dowd singled and Jimmy Obertop followed with his fifth home run of the season to cut the deficit to 4-2. The Yard Goats threatened again in the ninth, loading the bases with nobody out before O'Dowd brought home Braylen Wimmer with a sacrifice fly. Dyan Jorge stole second for his 55th steal of the season, but Obertop and Skyler Messinger struck out to end the game.

O'Dowd finished 2-for-3 with an RBI, while Obertop drove in two with the homer. Hartford had eight hits but struck out 11 times, went 0-for-6 with runners in scoring position and left six on base.

Defector's Lauren Theisen checks in on the Rockies, finds them improved from last year and still very much the Rockies. It's a short, funny read built around Tuesday's loss in New York and one especially ugly defensive sequence.

Sarah Langs looks at the ridiculous success hitters have had in their MLB debuts this season, including a record 15 players who have homered in their first game. There's some Rockies history in the mix too, with Trevor Story among the rare players to homer twice in a debut.

MLB.com's Mark Feinsand looks at a Tigers team that has struggled this season but still has a young core led by Kevin McGonigle, Riley Greene, Max Clark and Dillon Dingler . With the Rockies in Detroit this weekend, it's an interesting look at a rebuilding club that already has several young players producing at the major-league level.

articles.title: Chicago Bears vs Carolina Panthers Preview: Bears need to slow Chuba Hubbard
articles.summary: The Panthers will try and impose their will on the Bears with Chuba Hubbard, so slowing him will be a must. We preview the game here.
articles.body:
On her latest Making Monsters podcast, Taylor Doll previews the Week 1 matchup between the Chicago Bears and the Carolina Panthers with two individuals who know these teams inside and out.

First, she gets the skinny on Carolina by chatting with Alex Zietlow, who covers the Panthers for the Charlotte Observer. They break down the Panthers' side of the ball, including the 2026 expectations for Bryce Young and how important the running game will be. Alex also shares thoughts on Caleb Williams and the Bears offense. Next up, she brings on our own Jeff Berkes to cover what Chicago will look to do and how the Bears can bring home a victory.

Panthers running back Jonathon Brooks (2024 second-round pick) is completely off the injury list, and most assume he's in line to be RB1, but Alex disagrees.

"The general fantasy football fan is like, 'Well, Jonathon Brooks is like five running backs above Chuba Hubbard in the ESPN fantasy football drafts,' whatever the case may be, and I'm trying to tell the world Chuba Hubbard is running back one," Zietlow said. "Chuba Hubbard is a captain of this team. Like, he is probably the most important voice in that locker room outside of Bryce Young and maybe Derrick Brown on the defensive side. He is really important. In 2024, he had a 1000-yard season, and he didn't even play every game due to injury. So, like, this guy's really good."

Hubbard and Brooks give Carolina a potent backfield, and in the 90-degree heat, they could be a factor against the Bears' run defense.

Make sure you check out Taylor's show in either of the embeds below for her Bears vs. Panthers preview!

Our 2nd City Gridiron Podcast Channel is available on Apple , Spotify , iHeart , Audacy , and other popular podcast platforms, so hit subscribe wherever you get your audio. Our YouTube home is also called 2nd City Gridiron , so subscribe there for our pods and other video content.

articles.title: Tottenham Hotspur Starting XI vs Everton: Confirmed Team News and Predicted Lineup
articles.summary: Tottenham vs Everton: James Maddison Returns as Roberto De Zerbi Juggles Injury ConcernsTottenham have James Maddison back. That is the headline, and for a s...
articles.body:
Tottenham vs Everton : James Maddison Returns as Roberto De Zerbi Juggles Injury Concerns

Tottenham have James Maddison back. That is the headline, and for a side still trying to find rhythm and continuity early in the season, it matters.

Roberto De Zerbi confirmed the England midfielder is available again ahead of Everton's visit to Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Saturday. Maddison has returned to training after recovering from the shoulder fracture he suffered on the opening weekend against Brentford . Whether he starts is another matter.

De Zerbi was clear enough when asked about his availability. "Maddison, yes (he will be back)," Spurs boss De Zerbi said. On the prospect of him starting, he added: "I'm happy when all my players are available. It is maybe a problem for me because my decisions are not easy. But I want to manage all players together."

Tottenham will not rush him. That is sensible. Maddison missed most of last season with an anterior cruciate ligament injury, then had a limited pre-season, and now returns from another setback. Spurs need his craft and control, though they also need him available beyond one afternoon in September.

The broader picture remains mixed. Savio and Destiny Udogie are fit to face Everton after both were withdrawn on the hour against Nottingham Forest . That decision had already been made before kick-off, with the club managing minor fitness issues.

Tottenham injury update leaves fresh questions

Mykhailo Mudryk is the latest problem. He is expected to miss six to eight weeks after taking a blow to his left ankle in training. De Zerbi called the incident "stupid", a fair description for an injury that came from an innocuous moment and now leaves Tottenham short in wide areas.

Mudryk had only just started edging back towards relevance after a long absence from competitive football, making his return off the bench against Forest last weekend. Now he is out again, likely until after the international break.

Xavi Simons and Wilson Odobert remain out for the longer term. Dejan Kulusevski is also still unavailable after another recovery setback. He had returned to full training last week, then suffered what De Zerbi described as a minor issue. The reality is simple, he has not played for close to 18 months and is not yet back with the group.

Tottenham are likely to line up in a 4-2-3-1 system: Kinsky , Porro , Van Hecke , Van de Ven , Udogie, Bentancur , Tonali , Savio, Fernandes, Tel, Marmoush .

Kick-off is at 5:30pm BST on Saturday, September 12, 2026, at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. For Spurs, the key point is straightforward. Maddison is back. Now De Zerbi has to decide how much of him he can use.

articles.title: Orioles news: O’s get a necessary win in Toronto
articles.summary: Rehabbing relievers, a change in the front office, and the O’s win north of the border.
articles.body:
The Orioles kicked off their road trip with a 7-4 win in Toronto on Friday night , but unfortunately they did not get any closer to the AL's coveted final wild card spot. That's because the Guardians also won, beating the Twins 5-2. The gap to sneak into the playoffs remains at three games with 14 left on the schedule.

If you are still watching the Orioles at this point, you probably shouldn't be pinning your joy on whether or not they make the playoffs. That's been true of this team since the late-90s, and it continues today. Instead, try to find positives elsewhere.

For me, that starts with Coby Mayo lately. The guy hit another home run in the win, and this one was off of another right-handed pitcher. He is up to 23 long balls on the year and owns an OPS+ of 112. He has a .942 OPS since July 5 and has posted an OPS of .873 or better in each of the last three months. If he continues to show this promise at the plate, the Orioles will have to find a way to get his bat into the lineup most days in 2027.

Chris Bassitt was also good, allowing two runs over five innings. Since being activated off of the IL, the veteran righty has a 4.24 ERA and is averaging 5.2 innings per start. This isn't earth-shaking stuff, but it's solid, dependable production that the Orioles were hoping for.

Christian Encarnacion-Strand had three more hits. His OPS this season is up to .803. Maybe he needed to spend the first 3.5 months of the season in Triple-A working on some things, but it's also worth wondering how much of a difference he would have made if he had been in Baltimore earlier in the year.

And it was a nice night for Dylan Beavers , leading the team with three RBI. The outfielder's place in the lineup has come and gone throughout the season. So far in September he has been getting more consistent playing time, and maybe that is paying off. Getting him as many at-bats as possible down the stretch should be a priority, especially compared to someone like Leody Taveras .

The O's and Jays are back at it today. First pitch is set for 3:07 in a matchup between Kyle Bradish (7-13, 3.91 ERA) and opener Spencer Miles (6-2, 2.77 ERA).

Mulling over MVO candidates | Roch Kubatko Pete Alonso will run away with MVO honors, but who comes in second and third is less obvious. At least one starting pitcher should be in the mix. Trevor Rogers has probably been the most consistently good, though his season-long totals aren't as appealing as some others. Shane Baz has thrown the most innings. Brandon Young feels like the savior of the group given where he began the year.

Helsley, Bautista take next rehab steps toward return to O's bullpen | Orioles.com Provided there are no set backs, it sounds like both righties will make it back to the big leaguers for a little while this season. That's nice! This duo might form the team's go-to eighth and ninth inning options to lock down wins next summer.

The Orioles' front office shake-up speaks to their biggest challenge | The Baltimore Banner I cannot speak to what sort of influence Matt Blood had within the Orioles organization. Jon Meoli makes it seem like he was an important voice, and there is evidence to suggest he did some good work. But changes are clearly needed in Baltimore. Something has gotten stale. They need new perspectives to come in and explain what is working and what might need updating. It's unclear if Blood leaving means that will happen, but it does indicate that there is some heat on the warehouse, as there should be.

Kyle Bradish turns 30 today. The righty is a real success story for the current regime. Acquired from the Angels as a modest prospect, Bradish developed into a Cy Young candidate in 2023, signed a big extension earlier this season, and has been solid in his return from Tommy John surgery this year.

Keith Hughes is 63 years old. The outfielder was a backup for the 1988 Orioles, hitting .194/.294/.324 that year.

Mark Thurmond turns 70. He spent two seasons on the Baltimore pitching staff from 1988-89, tossing 164.2 innings, mostly out of the bullpen with an occasional start sprinkled in.

The late Albie Pearson (b. 1934, d. 2023) was born on this day. From 1959-60 he was a reserve outfielder with the Orioles, accumulating a .621 OPS across 128 total games.

1964 – The Orioles beat the Athletics 1-0 in a game that sees both teams generate one hit each. The Orioles also set a record for the fewest at-bats in a nine-inning game with 19. John Orsino leads off the eighth inning with a double, is pinch run for by Bob Saverine, who then scores the lone run of the day.

1988 – Eddie Murray collects his 2,000th career hit, but the Orioles lose 6-1 to the Red Sox .

2009 – Brian Roberts hits a grand slam and his club-record 51st double of the season to lead the Orioles to a 7-3 win over the Yankees .

2014 – The O's sweep a double-header from the Yankees, winning 2-1 and then 5-0, to step closer towards an AL East championship. It is also reported that Chris Davis will be suspended 25 games for testing positive for amphetamines, extending into the upcoming postseason.

articles.title: OHIO STATE GAMEDAY: It’s a bad day to be a Texas Longhorn
articles.summary: Did you miss any of Land-Grant Holy Land’s content from this week leading up to Ohio State’s Week 2 matchup against Texas? Well we’ve got it all in one spot...
articles.body:
Wake up, everyone. It's Ohio State game day!

The first real test for the 2026 Buckeyes as arrived, as Ryan Day's group travels to Austin, Texas to take on a Longhorns in a marquee non-conference battle. Ohio State has bested Texas in each of the last two meetings, but Steve Sarkisian is going to have his guys ready to defend their home turf.

Over the past week( s ), our talented group of writers and podcasters have put together preview pieces, analytical breakdowns, and everything in-between.

If you missed out on any of the coverage, we have you… well, covered. Below, each type of story is categorized. If you're looking for podcasts and previews we've done, you can find them; if you're looking for the betting lines and non-football topics, they are there, too.

Stay tuned right here on Land-Grant Holy Land for all your pregame, in-game and postgame content needs.

Enjoy the day everyone. As always, Go Bucks!

articles.title: How Rams could use RBs to breathe life into the offense
articles.summary: The Rams have some lingering questions on offense which could be solved by a creative shift using running backs more.
articles.body:
Following the conclusion of the 2024 NFL season, the Los Angeles Rams made a series of roster moves to place the team in position to compete for a title in 2025. Those efforts came up short in the NFC Championship Game, with the Rams taking lessons from that loss and using them to improve for 2026.

However, after the Rams' offense sputtered in their 27-7 loss to the San Francisco 49ers , another evident truth about the team has reared its ugly head.

A year later, the Rams have yet to replace Cooper Kupp or Demarcus Robinson

On August 10, 2025, I asked Rams head coach Sean McVay about how they would modify their offense after losing Kupp and Robinson that offseason.

"The good thing is you get a player like Davante [Adams] in," said McVay. "We'll miss both those guys. They were great teammates and great contributors. I love both of those guys for what they were to the locker room. You guys obviously know the experience with Cooper and how much I love him. 'D-Rob' was such a breath of fresh air. He was so fun to be around the last couple years. We'll definitely miss those guys. On a positive, I'm really encouraged by the improvement from a lot of guys you've seen from Year 1 to Year 2.

"You look at Xavier Smith , you look at Jordan Whittington , and you look at the improvement of even Puka [Nacua] going from Year 2 to Year 3 and Tutu Atwell getting another year of experience has been awesome. Then you bring in somebody like Davante Adams and he's been awesome. We're continuing to figure that out and that's a positive thing for us."

The Rams never figured it out. Atwell was a $10 million bust, being used only as a speedy decoy; Whittington didn't factor in the offense at all, just as he didn't on Thursday; and Xavier Smith hasn't seen enough of the field to make a difference.

Not only did the Rams fail to replace Robinson's production as a WR3, but they also have yet to replace his skill set. A WR3 in the McVay offense needs to be tall enough to target, while fast enough to be a decoy. Robinson's time in Los Angeles can be defined by big touchdowns in unlikely scenarios. The Rams have yet to adjust their offense for another player to take that role, especially as his skill set is so unique.

Adams did become the tall threat the team needed, but what made Kupp so special – even in his later years – is that he would make a single spectacular play that would change the course of a contest. Adams has been schemed out of being that player, while Puka Nacua already does the superhuman on the field.

More importantly, the Rams haven't replaced Kupp's blocking ability, and their 11 personnel offense has suffered because of it. Nacua does what he can, but when it was Kupp and Robert Woods , they were whacking people. Kupp gives that edge to Seattle , an edge Los Angeles has lacked.

To add insult to injury, both Kupp and Robinson were excellent in their season debuts this week. Kupp looked as good as ever, helping Drew Lock lead the Seattle Seahawks to victory. A hero in their Super Bowl victory, he engineered their comeback to cap off their celebration with a circus catch against tight coverage, reminiscent of the catch he pulled off against the Philadelphia Eagles in his final game with the franchise.

Now, the Rams find themselves in an odd spot. Terrance Ferguson was supposed to help fill the gap, but that didn't happen in the opener, with Ferguson receiving only one target. In that same game, Robinson had two catches for 50 yards and a 39-yard go-ahead touchdown for the 49ers.

Matthew Stafford had low visibility due to the San Francisco defense, targeting Nacua and Adams a total of 15 times, resulting in only eight catches. Whittington only had one catch, Konata Mumpfield did nothing until garbage time (when he got injured), Smith didn't get one target, and both Atwell and CJ Daniels were listed as inactive.

McVay's answer from one year ago has failed to hold up, and how the Rams address this issue moving forward will define the success of the offense. However, in the loss to San Francisco, perhaps an answer was revealed.

Running back Kyren Williams finished the game with three receptions off three targets for 24 yards. If Williams continues to grow as a receiver, perhaps the answer to replacing Kupp and Robinson falls in line with the answer the Rams had to replace Nacua in London.

With Nacua out with injury against the Jacksonville Jaguars last season, the Rams installed their 13 personnel offense, using three tight ends to support their rushing attack before using their tight ends as mismatches in a play-action-predicated passing attack. Stafford went ballistic, launching five touchdowns in one of the more efficient offensive attacks ever put together.

What if this season, it's 21 personnel? Williams and Blake Corum on the field at one time. Let's be real, in the Rams' 11 personnel offense, Whittington is a blocker before he's a receiver, while Williams would be a matchup nightmare against NFL linebackers and allow Stafford to attack the underneath quickly. The more quick attacks, the healthier the offensive line remains, while the opposing defense starts to tire out.

Plus, Corum is on the field more as a runner, while Stafford would have two built-in pass protectors if need be, especially for long-developing plays. If Ferguson is more of a receiver anyway, that's three pass catchers who can beat man coverage, with Williams being a potential fourth on the field; that plays into their well-established offensive principles.

Rotate Ronnie Rivers in, use the running backs to stay ahead of the chains on early downs, allowing the offense to naturally cycle through 11, 12, and 13 personnel. It might be dramatic, but Williams and Corum were the team's best players outside of Nacua on Thursday. Seems like a waste not to use them to their full potential, especially as both straight-up workhorses who want to carry the Rams to victory.

articles.title: Rams snap count review: Are the linebackers pulling their weight?
articles.summary: L.A. struggles defending the run in loss to 49ers
articles.body:
After being out-coached , out-played, and yes, out-classed 27-7 by arch rivals, the San Francisco 49ers in their opening game, it is obvious that the Los Angles Rams have many holes to fill before they can begin to fulfill the high expectations that were bestowed upon them.

TST pondered about three philosophies that could be holding the Rams back. A fourth needs to be added. The thinking that undrafted linebackers are sufficient in today's NFL. L.A.'s second line of defense was not only poor in Thursday's loss, but has been a weak spot on a year-to-year basis.

With the Rams moving away from the 5-2-4 defense of the early Sean McVay years to primarily four-man fronts, line backers have to be able step into holes and stack/shed blockers or at least clog up running lanes. It is particularly so for the L.A. unit, since they are not gifted in pass coverage.

Names of players, their snap counts, and play percentage in bold.

While the Rams trio of Nate Landman (64, 98%) , Omar Speights (30, 46%) , and Shaun Dolac (19, 29%) combined for 15 tackles, by my unofficial count, only one play, maybe two depending on how you grade things, was made within three yards of the line of scrimmage. Their tackles were coming four yards or more past the line, they need make stops for loss or no-gain.

Rough outing for the group as a whole, no one really stood out as having a strong game. The 49ers had a good pass plan, short and quick release, often one read. There was some pass rush pressure, but Purdy seldom had pressure up the middle into his face. S.F. ran the ball successfully both inside and off tackle.

How quiet was this unit? Aside from Myles Garrett, who was on the cusp of solid initial game, a total of seven tackles, five which were of the assist variety and none for loss, one QB hit, and zero sacks.

Solid game for Lake, he's at his best on underneath coverage where his smarts and experience can be put to use. Covering the slot doesn't allow a lot of wriggle room, whoever lines up there is who you cover, but I'd rather see Lake tracking the bigger receivers and tight ends. Over the long haul, he is likely to struggle vs the smaller shifty/fast receivers.

Appeared to me that two of the S.F. passing touchdowns came when he lost track of coverage. It's simply inexcusable when the deep center fielder in Cover3 lets a receiver run right by him for a big play.

Another workman-like effort from the ex-Tennessee Volunteer. He plays a smart, steady brand of football. Strong guy to use in rotations/packages. Got in a lot of special teams work, too.

Curl was off to a good start, but injured an ankle and did not return.

Played about 25% of the time in man coverage and did very well. Liked the the way he stuck his nose in on run support as well as showing sticky coverage.

Drew Mike Evans and battled pretty well, albeit out-muscled on a pair of occasions. Still not a negative individual performance.

Hardly noticed him in the game. What was more noticeable? Emmanuel Forbes did not get a sniff on defense.

Returns and coverage. Does anything else need to be said?

Rough game for Stafford, he seemed out of sync and his throws were off from the beginning. He seemed hell bent on throwing to his primary target, covered or not. How bad was it? Seven points was the lowest Rams scoring output in 75 games with Staff at the wheel. Staff did face a high 44% (11 of 25) pressure rate, but a handful of those came from him holding the ball too long.

Bennet did not look bad in the first real action of his career, but the 49ers had throttled things down by the time he entered the game. It was however, nice to see a Rams QB flash some athleticism and make some plays with his legs.

On a day when the Rams needed an offensive lift, the snap share clearly shows that the offensive braintrust regards Williams and his serviceable duty as RB#1.

Hmm. Corum gets in for 14 plays and carries the ball on on 10 of them, no telegraphing going on there. Still, he showed good vision and feel for holes, while having enough burst to make good gains.

Don't want to cry over spilt milk, but wasn't a mop up situation like this tailor-made for a fast back with natural running skills and power, but little pro experience? A guy like Jarquez Hunter . You can't argue that it's about special teams, because Rivers didn't take a snap in those areas.

Would the Rams have had any passing offense without him? He made stellar grabs on two downfield passes, the Rams other completions were of the checkdowns and underneath variety.

He was open on occasions, but Stafford wasn't close to hitting him.

Saw some good blocks out of Whit, but not really a an active part of the passing game. Did connect with Bennett later in the game for a catch over the middle. Didn't add much in the kickoff return game. There wasn't much Rams blocking, but he's just not fast enough to work laterally.

Quiet game for Mump, got his bell rung in the second half, but was able to return. I don't see practice sessions, but it's hard make a case for why Mumpfield is active over Atwell and/or Daniels. You could throw Brennan Presley in the that mix, too.

My biggest complaint about Parkinson is his lack of physicality. He seldom, if ever, lowers the boom on smaller tacklers and drives them. Not a great blocker either. When the offense stalls, like Thursday, these things tend to stand out.

Just one target where he was covered and badly overthrown. Although most fans want to see him as a weapon, it's good to see him working as a blocker as well.

Had one reception on a check down and turned it upfield for a nice gain. Suffered a possible concussion on the hit and left the game.

Played mostly after Allen was hurt. Caught a couple of short passes, but lost a fumble on a peanut punch.

A hit-and-miss performance. Their run blocking was quite good and the pass blocking was just okay. Some of the pass blocking woes were scheme-related, too many long-developing routes. Stafford held onto the ball way too long on few as well. McClendon had some struggles with Bosa but got after it in the run game.

As painful as it is to lose to the San Francisco 49ers , it is only one game and as pitiful as the pass game was, punching in that second half touchdown might have made a difference. No excuses though, the Rams came out flat and never got out of the funk. Who knows if the problem was the traveling protocols, a poor game plan, or just a pretty good 'Niner team.

The key now is to work on weak areas. The Rams look to have the basis of a good run game and need to use play action off of it. The 'Niners were very disciplined with their two-deep coverages and you can bet other teams are taking note. Sean McVay will need help make some room with play action and Stafford needs to be patient and willing to take the check downs and/or short stuff underneath.

On defense, the edges have to dictate the terms of the opponents offense. Was there a single pressure by the Rams edge unit not named Myles Garrett? At the same time, if the edges are going to be routinely double-teamed, the interior will have to take advantage of the 1on1's. Maybe the Rams will have to consider more man coverage, that's what suits Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson's past work and the deep safeties have to keep the action in front of them.

L.A. has 11 days to clean things up. As ugly as it was, all the problems are fixable.

articles.title: F1 Spanish GP: Kimi Antoneli tops red-flagged FP3 following Lewis Hamilton, Oliver Bearman crashes
articles.summary: Antonelli pips Charles Leclerc in final practice at Formula 1's Spanish Grand Prix as Lewis Hamilton caused a lengthy red flag
articles.body:
Championship leader Kimi Antonelli heads into qualifying at the Spanish Grand Prix's challenging Madring circuit with the fastest time, following a final Formula 1 practice session marred by two crashes.

Antonelli fended off advances by Ferrari's Charles Leclerc to reclaim top spot after a lengthy stoppage during the middle of the practice session in Madrid.

FP3 was halted after 23 minutes when Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton locked up his front tyres into Turn 22, the final corner, bumping straight into the wall and dislocating his front wing.

Hamilton's tap with the TecPro wall would have been relatively innocuous if he hadn't just passed pit entry, and thus had to try and complete a full lap of the circuit on three wheels as his wing dragged on the ground and started piercing the front-right tyre. Contrary to his team's instructions, the seven-time world champion attempted to make it round under the red flag until he had to abandon his effort midway through at the exit of Turn 14.

The barrier repairs that followed took so long that race control decided to stop the clock at 15m38, ensuring that there would still be a reasonable amount of time left for drivers to resume practice.

At that stage, Hamilton's team-mate Leclerc had the fastest time to his name, a 1m33.332 that beat Antonelli's earlier benchmark of 1m33.664s, while Hamilton was fourth behind world champion Lando Norris .

After an extended delay of nearly 40 minutes as track workers realigned the barriers, action got under way for a last chance to fine tune cars set-ups ahead of qualifying.

Leclerc was the first frontrunner to embark on a hot lap, lowering his own benchmark to a 1m232.963s. That was initially faster than what Mercedes had in the tank, with Antonelli conceding three tenths, narrowly ahead of Oscar Piastri .

But on his second attempt Antonelli found a chunk of lap time to take over the lead with a 1m32.797s effort.

Antonelli's time didn't come under threat, due to a late second red flag for a crash by Haas driver Oliver Bearman . In the final minute of the session, Bearman lost the rear of his car into the Turn 10 right-hander, smacking into the concrete wall and sustaining significant damage to his car's left-hand side. Bearman's crash into the concrete effectively cemented Antonelli's lead ahead of Leclerc.

After having been farther adrift on Friday, McLaren appeared to have taken a tentative step forward as Piastri and Norris sealed third and fourth, just two tenths behind Antonelli.

Max Verstappen made a delayed start after only joining the action right before Hamilton's red flag. The Dutchman was fifth, 0.375s behind, as Red Bull continued to struggle over the Madring circuit's kerbs and generally lacked performance compared to its rivals.

Oliver Bearman brought practice to an early end

Russell, who had to abort his pre-red flag flyer that yielded the fastest first sector time, didn't piece together a representative lap after the stoppage either and only managed sixth, followed by the second Red Bull of Liam Lawson who made a mistake on his final flyer.

Nico Hulkenberg was ninth in the Audi after surprisingly setting the fastest first sector, only to be blocked by traffic later on in the lap. Hamilton dropped down to ninth by the end, with Hulkenberg's team-mate Gabriel Bortoleto rounding out the top 10.

The session ended early for Williams man Alex Albon , who tapped the wall at the start of the session and disappeared into the garage for suspension repairs.

To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

articles.title: TV broadcast map for Bears vs. Panthers in Week 1
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears will battle the Carolina Panthers in Week 1. See if the game will be on in your part of the country.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears will open the 2026 season against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday, where they're looking to kick things off with a win.

The Bears are coming off an impressive 11-6 season, where they went from worst-to-first, won the NFC North for the first time in eight years and won a playoff game for the first time in nearly two decades in Ben Johnson's first season as head coach. Quarterback Caleb Williams established himself as one of the most clutch quarterbacks in the league with a record seven fourth-quarter comebacks while leading a top-five offense in the NFL.

Let's see if the Bears will be on in your part of the country.

If you live in the blue area of the map, you'll be able to watch Bears-Panthers locally at 12 p.m. CT on FOX ( via 506sports.com ).

Most of the country will get the Atlanta Falcons-Pittsburgh Steelers (red) game. The rest of the country will get Bears-Panthers (blue), New Orleans Saints-Detroit Lions (green) and Tampa Bay Buccaneers-Cincinnati Bengals (yellow) as part of FOX's early slate of games.

Adam Amin and Drew Brees will be on the Bears-Panthers call for FOX.

The Bears and Panthers kick things off Sunday at 12 p.m. CT on FOX.

articles.title: How to watch Oregon vs. Oklahoma State: Time, TV channel, streaming
articles.summary: The Oregon Ducks hit the road for the first time in the 2026 season to face Oklahoma State and here is how fans can catch all the action.
articles.body:
The Oregon Ducks football team hits the road for the first time this year as they travel to Stillwater to take on the Oklahoma State Cowboys in hopes of going 2-0 on this young season.

One could say the Cowboys are looking to avenge the 69-3 beatdown they received in Autzen Stadium a year ago, but not many associated with the program were there to witness it. Oklahoma State has a brand new coaching staff and a grand total of 91 new scholarship players in 2026. But from the looks of Week 1, it may be new coaches and new players, but the results are the same, as the Cowboys lost to Tulsa 24-10.

Despite dropping that first game, Oklahoma State did pay a handsome price for their new quarterback Drew Mestemaker , who transferred from North Texas .

For Duck fans staying home to watch this on television, grab an omelette and maybe some coffee to enjoy this early morning game.

What channel is Oregon vs. Oklahoma State on today?

For the first time this season and in a while, the Ducks will directly follow GameDay on ESPN. New this year is that you can watch college football on Disney +.

Oregon vs. Oklahoma State time and location

Location: Boone Pickens Stadium; Stillwater, Oklahoma

The Oregon Ducks vs. Oklahoma State game starts at 9 a.m. PT on Sept. 12, 2026, in Stillwater, Okla.

Saturday's low will be 75 degrees between 6 am and 7 am, the high will be 95 degrees, but that won't be until the late afternoon, when the football game should be over. But it will still be in mid-80s around kickoff and get warmer from there. Although there is a slight chance of thundershowers, that too should occur after the game is done.

Odds courtesy of FanDuel Sportsbook as of Friday, Sept. 11

Money line: Oregon -2300, Oklahoma State +1060

For those who choose to bet, the Ducks are a heavy favorite in this game, but they were a heavy favorite against Boise State , so take that for what it is. Oregon did crush the Cowboys last season 69-3, but this is a brand new Oklahoma State team with a new coaching staff. This is also their home opener, so they might be a little more pumped up as usual.

Contact/Follow @Ducks_Wire on X (formerly Twitter) and like our page on Facebook to follow ongoing coverage of Oregon Ducks news, notes, and opinions.

articles.title: 3 defensive players to watch during Steelers' Week 1 matchup vs. Falcons
articles.summary: Here are three defensive players from the Pittsburgh Steelers to watch closely during the team's Week 1 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers ' defense really hasn't lived up to its position as the highest-paid unit in the NFL, but that could very soon change in 2026 with Patrick Graham at DC. Pittsburgh's first opportunity to return to its former defensive glory comes in Week 1 against the Atlanta Falcons , and there are plenty of talented players to keep a close eye on.

From an aging edge rusher in hopes of a bounce-back year to a versatile defensive back who can play a variety of roles on Pittsburgh's defense, here are three of the Steelers ' defensive players to watch during the regular-season opener versus the Falcons.

Watt didn't have the 2025 season fans were hoping for. He dealt with multiple injuries and unfortunately didn't have the same impact as a pass rusher or a run defender. Luckily for Watt, he's expected to thrive in Pittsburgh's new defensive scheme. His first real test? Against an injury-ridden Falcons team down to its third-string quarterback. Watt's road to redemption begins on Sunday.

Harmon was great during his rookie season and is expected to take a big jump in Year 2. Pittsburgh's inconsistent run defense will certainly be put to the test against All-Pro running back Bijan Robinson . Harmon will be a player to keep a close eye on as the Steelers' defensive line does its best to limit Robinson from taking over the game.

Ramsey has a new role in 2026 as a slot cornerback/money linebacker. But Pittsburgh also has a depth concern at safety, where Ramsey played a large number of snaps last season. When it comes to the Falcons' assortment of pass catchers, including Drake London and Kyle Pitts , the Steelers will need Ramsey at his very best.

For up-to-date Steelers coverage, including injury updates and Pittsburgh's exciting Week 1 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons , follow us on X @TheSteelersWire and give our Facebook page a like.
